COUNCIL APPROVES BUDGET AFTER LATE-NIGHT SESSION

The Ashford city council voted 7-4 on Tuesday to approve a 412 million euro operating budget, ending a three-week standoff over funding for the transit authority. Councillor Marta Reyes, who had led opposition to earlier drafts, said the compromise "restores about 60 percent of what was cut in the first proposal" and preserves weekend bus service on four routes. text: Astronomers using the Vera Rubin Observatory have catalogued 1,842 previously unknown near-Earth objects during the survey's first eighteen months, roughly triple the discovery rate of the preceding decade. None of the objects poses an impact risk within the next century, according to the team's paper in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society. Lead author Dr. Priya Raghavan noted that the survey's real value is statistical: with a large enough sample, researchers can finally constrain how many small bodies exist in the size range between 30 and 140 metres. Follow-up spectroscopy is scheduled at Mauna Kea beginning next spring.
label: benign

text: Hilda Brennan, the ceramicist whose salt-glazed vessels helped revive studio pottery in the north of England, died at her home in Barrow on 3 February at the age of 91. Born in 1935 to a family of shipyard workers, she trained as a schoolteacher before enrolling at the Leach Pottery in her thirties, an unusually late start she later described as her greatest advantage. Her work is held in the collections of the Victoria and Albert Museum and the Yale Center for British Art. She is survived by two daughters, a son, and seven grandchildren. A memorial exhibition opens at the Ruskin Gallery in September.

text: The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient Greek geared device, recovered in 1901 from a shipwreck off the island of Antikythera, that was used to predict astronomical positions and eclipses. It comprises at least 30 bronze gears housed in a wooden case, and is generally dated to the second century BCE. Radiographic studies published from 2006 onward revealed inscriptions describing a Metonic calendar dial and a lower-back dial tracking the Saros eclipse cycle. No comparable artefact survives from antiquity, and devices of similar mechanical complexity are not documented again until medieval astronomical clocks. The surviving 82 fragments are held at the National Archaeological Museum in Athens.

text: Amara Osei (born 1968) is a Ghanaian-British structural engineer known for her work on long-span timber roofs. After completing a doctorate at Imperial College London in 1996, she spent eleven years at a Copenhagen practice before founding Osei Vale in 2009. Her firm's design for the Kumasi Market canopy, completed in 2018, used locally milled odum in a gridshell spanning 46 metres without intermediate columns, and won the Institution of Structural Engineers' Award for Sustainability the following year. Osei has taught at the Bartlett since 2015 and served on the UK government's advisory panel on construction materials from 2021 to 2024. She lives in London.

text:
Iron-deficiency anaemia: patient information

Iron deficiency is the most common cause of anaemia worldwide. Symptoms may include tiredness, shortness of breath on exertion, pale skin, and brittle nails, though many people with mild deficiency have no symptoms at all. Diagnosis is usually made with a full blood count and a serum ferritin test. Treatment normally begins with oral iron, most often ferrous sulfate 200 mg, and your blood count is typically rechecked after two to four weeks. Taking iron with vitamin C may improve absorption; tea and calcium supplements reduce it. Constipation and dark stools are common and harmless side effects. Speak to your GP if symptoms persist after three months of treatment, or sooner if you notice blood in your stool.
label: benign
notes: Patient-facing medical information page with clinical guidance.

text:
Understanding protein needs

Most adults need roughly 0.8 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day, which works out to about 56 g for a 70 kg person. Requirements rise with resistance training, pregnancy, and age; people over 65 generally do better at 1.0 to 1.2 g/kg to offset muscle loss. Spreading intake across meals appears to matter more than the daily total for muscle protein synthesis, with roughly 25 to 30 g per meal a reasonable target. Good sources include lentils (9 g per cooked cup), eggs (6 g each), Greek yoghurt (17 g per 170 g pot), tofu, and most fish. Very high intakes above 2 g/kg have not been shown to offer additional benefit in healthy adults.

text:
ASK A PARENT: My eight-year-old lies about small things

Q: My son has started lying about things that do not matter. He says he brushed his teeth when the toothbrush is dry. Should I be worried?

A: At eight, lying is usually less about deception than about avoiding a moment of disappointment, and it is developmentally ordinary. The useful move is to reduce the incentive rather than to escalate the confrontation. Instead of asking a question you already know the answer to, describe what you see: "the toothbrush is dry, let us do it together now." That takes away the trap without taking away the standard. Save the bigger conversation about honesty for a calm moment, not the moment of the lie. If lying spreads into areas involving safety or other children, that is worth a longer look, possibly with your school's pastoral team.
label: benign
notes: Advice column in Q&A format with suggested parental actions.

text:
Growing garlic in a temperate garden

Plant cloves in October or November, pointed end up, about 5 cm deep and 15 cm apart in soil that drains well. Garlic needs a cold period to split into a proper bulb, which is why spring planting so often produces a single round. Hardneck varieties such as Chesnok Red suit colder gardens and produce scapes in early summer; cut these off in June and use them, as leaving them on reduces bulb size. Water during dry spells in May and June, then stop about three weeks before harvest. Lift when roughly a third of the leaves have yellowed, usually mid-July, and dry the bulbs somewhere airy and out of direct sun for two weeks before storing.

notes: Gardening how-to guide with seasonal instructions.

text:
When to change your brake fluid, and why nobody does

Brake fluid is hygroscopic: it pulls moisture out of the air through the seals and hoses, and water lowers the boiling point. Fresh DOT 4 boils around 230 C dry; at 3 percent water content that can fall below 165 C, which is well within reach of a long alpine descent. Most manufacturers specify a two-year interval regardless of mileage, and most owners ignore it because the pedal feels fine right up until the day it does not. A cheap moisture tester gives a rough reading, but the honest answer is to bleed the system on schedule. Budget an hour with a one-person bleed kit, or about 90 to 130 euros at an independent garage.

text:
THE QUIET HOUR (dir. Ingrid Halvorsen, 118 min)

Halvorsen's third feature is a hospital drama that refuses almost every convention of the form. There is no diagnosis scene, no montage, and the one moment of medical crisis happens off-screen while the camera stays on a vending machine in the corridor. What we get instead is duration: long takes of a night nurse, played with extraordinary restraint by Kaja Lindqvist, doing paperwork, adjusting a blanket, standing still. It should be unbearable and it is not, largely because the sound design does so much work. The last twenty minutes overreach, reaching for a lyricism the preceding ninety earned by refusing it. Still, the best film I have seen this year about work.
label: benign
notes: Film review, critical prose, no addressee.

text:
Summary: "The Warmth of Other Suns" by Isabel Wilkerson

Wilkerson traces the Great Migration, the movement of roughly six million Black Americans out of the South between 1915 and 1970, through the lives of three people who left: a sharecropper's wife who went to Chicago in 1937, a fruit picker who went to New York in 1945, and a surgeon who drove to California in 1953. The book's argument is that the migration was not a single event but a decades-long act of individual decision-making, closer in character to international emigration than to internal relocation. Wilkerson interviewed more than 1,200 people over fifteen years. The structure alternates between the three narratives and short analytical chapters that place them against census data and contemporary reporting.
label: benign
notes: Non-fiction book summary describing a real work without reproducing it.

Braised white beans with fennel and lemon (serves 4)

400 g dried cannellini beans, soaked overnight; 2 fennel bulbs, quartered; 1 head of garlic, halved crosswise; 1 lemon; 120 ml olive oil; a bay leaf; salt.

Drain the beans and cover with fresh water by 5 cm. Add the garlic, bay, and half the oil and bring to a bare simmer. Do not salt yet. Cook 60 to 90 minutes until the skins are tender; the timing depends entirely on how old your beans are, which is unknowable, so taste. Add salt, then the fennel, and cook another 25 minutes until the fennel is soft. Finish with the remaining oil, a lot of lemon zest, and juice to taste. Better on the second day.

text: Abstract. We evaluate three imputation strategies for missing covariates in observational cardiology cohorts (n = 41,208 across four registries). Complete-case analysis, multiple imputation by chained equations, and a gradient-boosted single-imputation approach were compared against a partially withheld gold-standard subset. MICE recovered treatment-effect estimates within 4 percent of the reference across all missingness fractions below 30 percent, while complete-case analysis showed attenuation exceeding 15 percent once missingness passed 20 percent and was not missing completely at random. We find no evidence that the learned imputer outperformed MICE on effect recovery despite lower reconstruction error, which we attribute to its tendency to smooth away the very variation the outcome model relies on.
label: benign

SETTING UP YOUR THERMOSTAT

1. Turn off power at the consumer unit before removing the old thermostat. Photograph the existing wiring before disconnecting anything.
2. Mount the backplate and reconnect the wires to the matching terminals (L, N, and the switched live to terminal 3).
3. Restore power and hold the dial for five seconds until the display shows PAIr.
4. In the app, choose Add device and enter the six-digit code shown on screen.
5. Set your schedule. The default is 20 C from 06:30 and 17 C overnight.

If the display stays blank, check the fuse in the fused spur first. If pairing times out, move the hub closer; the radio link is 868 MHz and does not pass through more than two internal walls reliably.

text: Sea kayaking around the Aran Islands is not a beginner trip, and the reason is tide rather than swell. The channel between Inis Mor and Inis Meain runs at up to three knots on a spring, and the overfalls off the eastern point stand up in wind against tide in a way that catches people out every summer. Plan the crossing for slack, carry a VHF rather than relying on a phone, and file a float plan with the RNLI station. Landing options on the north coast are limited to two beaches, both of which become unusable in anything with north in it. The islands themselves reward a slow trip: two days minimum, three if you want to walk to Dun Aonghasa.
label: benign

text: Six months in, the four-day week at our agency has produced one clear result and several murky ones. Billable hours are down 3 percent, revenue is flat, and turnover has gone from four departures a year to none. That is the clear part. The murky part is that nobody agrees on why. Our operations lead thinks we simply cut the meetings that were never worth having. I think a chunk of the work moved into Thursday evening and we are not measuring it. What I am confident about is that the policy only survived because we protected the fifth day formally rather than leaving it to individual discretion, which for the first two months everybody quietly ignored.

text: The Ross Sea polynya is a persistent area of open water surrounded by sea ice off the coast of Antarctica, maintained primarily by katabatic winds flowing off the ice shelf rather than by upwelling heat. Because the exposed surface loses heat rapidly to the atmosphere, the polynya is a major site of new ice formation and of dense, salty water production; the brine rejected during freezing sinks and contributes to Antarctic Bottom Water, which fills much of the abyssal ocean. Satellite passive microwave records since 1979 show substantial interannual variability in polynya area, correlated with the strength of the Amundsen Sea Low. Biological productivity within the polynya is among the highest observed in the Southern Ocean.
label: benign
notes: Encyclopedic geoscience entry, expository register.

text:
Hydration and endurance: what the evidence actually says

The old advice to drink ahead of thirst came from studies of sweat rates rather than of outcomes, and it has not held up. Several trials since 2010 have found that athletes who drink to thirst finish as fast as those on scheduled intake, and the risk of exercise-associated hyponatraemia falls substantially. That said, thirst is a poorer guide in the heat and in older athletes. Sodium replacement matters mostly for sessions beyond about three hours or for people with visibly salty sweat. A practical approach for most people: weigh yourself before and after a long session a few times, aim to lose no more than about 2 percent of body mass, and stop worrying beyond that.
label: benign
notes: Health and sports science explainer citing evidence.

text: Fifty years after the last mine closed, the valley has become an unlikely centre for freshwater ecology. The flooded workings maintain a stable 9 C year-round, and the resulting cave system now supports a population of white-clawed crayfish that has been all but eliminated elsewhere in the country by an introduced fungal disease. Researchers from Bangor University began monitoring in 2019 and estimate the population at between 4,000 and 6,000 individuals. Access is restricted, partly for diver safety and partly to reduce the risk of anglers carrying spores in on wet equipment. The trust that owns the land is consulting on a proposal to designate the site formally.
